system: You are a careful research assistant.
prompt:
Each item below is a decision point from an AI-safety research project (context and question), followed by what the team actually decided and a verbatim quote from their write-up. Restate the team's decision as one option in a multiple-choice item. The other options were written separately in a fixed form; the style example shows that form (it belongs to a DIFFERENT decision, so take only its form and level of detail from it, never its content).

Rules:
- Faithful: the same decision the team took, its core choice, nothing added. If the decision has several parts, keep the part that answers the question.
- Same level of abstraction as the context: refer to the setup in the context's own terms, and turn study-specific details the context does not mention (model names, dataset names, exact numbers, coined terms, odd specifics) into plain descriptions.
- Do not make it sound more careful, expert, idiosyncratic or polished than the style example, and add no reason for it.
- Form: exactly one sentence; imperative, present tense ("Run ...", "Report ...", "Treat ..."); between 155 and 180 characters; no digits (write any number in words); no first person (we, our, us, I, my, me); no names of people, labs, papers, models or datasets; no coined name for the phenomenon; no justification clause and no hedging.

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "option": str}]}

ITEMS:

=== key 56755b305a8f
Context: A researcher who had presented a paper on a fast uncertainty-estimation method for classification with Bayesian deep networks was writing a retrospective on the conference experience. He regarded the paper as technically solid, but felt the paper and presentation had not been sufficiently explicit about what the method can and cannot do.
Question: How should the researcher characterize the method's usefulness and limitations in his write-up?
What the team decided: Scoped the claim narrowly: the method is only useful when it must be very fast, and other approaches are probably better in most other cases
Quote: In short, I think the concept presented in the paper is only useful when your method needs to be very very fast. In most other circumstances, other approaches are probably just better.
Style example (different decision): State each limitation explicitly in the write-up and in future presentations, pairing every capability claim with its corresponding boundary case and the assumptions it rests on.

=== key 0c5ba8644a71
Context: A researcher reflecting on his conference paper on a fast uncertainty-estimation method concluded he had not been sufficiently explicit about what the method can and cannot do. Facing the question of how to communicate the work's limitations in his write-up and future presentations, he needed to decide how explicitly to spell out the method's shortcomings.
Question: How explicitly should the researcher state the limitations of his method?
What the team decided: Added an 'Honest thoughts of the first author' section to the poster that states the limitations explicitly
Quote: Therefore, on my poster, I added a section called “Honest thoughts of the first author” to make my thoughts more explicit.
Style example (different decision): Extend the approach with a conditional adversarial generator for images, moving directly to the more expressive model family for the next stage of the investigation.

=== key dedcfc864a5d
Context: A researcher had previously tested, in a bachelor thesis, whether inverting the classification process by backpropagating through generative models works, using recurrent sequence models as the generators. They now wanted to extend the approach beyond sequential data to other data types such as images. They were looking for a generative modeling approach suited to this next stage.
Question: Which generative model should the researcher use to extend the inverse classification approach to non-sequential data?
What the team decided: Chose to explore conditional GANs as the generative model for Inverse Classification
Quote: One of the open questions was whether using other generative networks might yield better results.
Style example (different decision): Evaluate inverse classification across several periodically saved snapshots and both input pathways, reporting accuracy per snapshot to separate training-stage effects from the inversion signal.

=== key fc29032de07d
Context: A researcher was exploring whether inverse classification works with conditional adversarial generative models for images. In these models, both the generator and discriminator receive class labels as one-hot vectors, and the generator additionally takes a noise vector. Training of the generator does not necessarily improve with more iterations, so model snapshots were saved periodically during training.
Question: How should the researcher extract class-relevant signal from the trained generative model to evaluate the inverse classification idea?
What the team decided: D2
Quote: The best model was chosen by visual inspection, i.e. I just checked whether the images generated when inputting all classes and some noise look reasonable.
Style example (different decision): Treat the near-perfect reconstruction as confirmation that the inversion procedure converges, and attribute the modest accuracy gains to design choices like update rates.

=== key 1dcbcc8a8219
Context: A researcher ran several variants of an inverse classification procedure that iteratively updates a generator's inputs using gradients. Across experiments, the models were able to reconstruct the target images nearly perfectly, yet the resulting classification accuracies were only modestly above baseline and shifted only slightly with design changes like update rates and delayed updates.
Question: How should the researcher interpret the fact that the model reconstructs target images nearly perfectly?
What the team decided: Interpreted near-perfect reconstructions as showing the gradient updates yield meaningful results, while separately noting classification accuracy remained poor
Quote: As shown in the image in experiments the reconstructions of the image are nearly perfect. Therefore the gradient updates yield meaningful results.
Style example (different decision): Conclude that the technique shows a small effect on a feasibility benchmark and that the results are consistent with a working method while remaining preliminary pending broader validation.

=== key 533f34878636
Context: A researcher conducted exploratory experiments testing whether a gradient-based inversion of classification works with adversarial image generators, using a simple benchmark dataset as a feasibility check. The results showed small but real accuracy gains under some configurations, with code openly available. The write-up frames the work as exploratory rather than a full study.
Question: How strongly should the researcher state the conclusion about whether the technique works?
What the team decided: D6
Quote: I just wanted to get a broad intuition whether GANs can be used for IC. It does not fulfill the requirements of rigorous research that a submission to a scientific journal or conference would involve.
Style example (different decision): Update only the noise vector with gradient information, keeping the one-hot class vector fixed as the conditioning signal the inversion is meant to recover.

=== key 458913a7b19c
Context: A researcher set up a conditional adversarial generator that takes two inputs: a one-hot class vector and a noise vector. Their inverse classification method works by updating inputs via gradient information, and the generator was trained on a simple 10-class image dataset used as a feasibility test.
Question: Which of the generator's inputs should the researcher update with gradient information during inverse classification?
What the team decided: Initially kept noise fixed and updated only the class vector, then switched to also optimizing the noise input
Quote: At first I thought it would be reasonable to keep the noise input fixed and only update the class vector. However, I realized quickly that this produced pretty bad results
Style example (different decision): Use plain gradient descent with a fixed step size first, then compare against an adaptive optimizer on the same benchmark to check the choice does not drive the effect.

=== key cf34e563af58
Context: A researcher was running inverse classification experiments by iteratively optimizing a conditional generator's inputs via gradients on a 10-class image benchmark. Having settled on which inputs to update, they needed to pick an optimization algorithm for this iterative gradient-based procedure.
Question: Which optimizer should the researcher use for the iterative gradient-based input optimization?
What the team decided: Chose Adam over other optimizers such as SGD
Quote: I also tested other optimizers such as SGD but Adam turned out to yield the best results.
Style example (different decision): Describe the method as a practical fast uncertainty estimator and note briefly that it is approximate, without cataloging every case where the approximation could degrade.
